payload: task_claim's re-entrant-claim discriminator uses owner_client_session, not owner_session -- discovered live 2026-08-14T09:3xZ by a po sub-agent that hit claimed:false with current_holder.owner_client_session matching its OWN session id but current_holder.owner_session belonging to a DIFFERENT concurrent same-session po sub-agent (peer subagent under the same router session, distinct process). Following the documented re-entrant rule (task_claim/dispatch-claim SKILL.md: claimed:false + current_holder.owner_client_session == own session -> treat as re-entrant, task_heartbeat and proceed) caused the po sub-agent to heartbeat-EXTEND a PEER's lock instead of detecting a genuine collision -- its own subsequent task_release then correctly no-op'd (released:0) since the lock was never actually its own. This affects every PRE-CLAIM/task_claim call fleet-wide that relies on owner_client_session as the re-entrancy discriminator, any time two sub-agents spawned from the same coordinating session (background Agent() calls, e.g. concurrent po/qa/developer sessions this same tick) race on the same task_id. Root cause not yet designed -- likely needs owner_session (unique per process/subagent) added as a second discriminator field, re-entrant treatment should require BOTH owner_client_session AND owner_session to match, not owner_client_session alone. Worth an architect-level design pass since this touches the core task-lock coordination primitive used by every agent type's PRE-CLAIM protocol, not a narrow single-flow fix. Source: po sub-agent (ac362246d1ed5d95c) triage of the rag-service memory incident, flagged in its own completion report, not yet minted as a tracked board row -- dev-team surfacing via signal for po's next triage pass rather than spawning a dedicated cycle immediately, since it is a design-correctness finding, not an active incident.
